Figure 1:Adaptive multi-modal reasoning with visual imagination.Conventional VLMs perceive multimodal inputs but reason entirely in text.
AVTR adaptively harnesses the complementary strengths of visual imagination
and textual reasoning according to the perceptual and inferential demands of the
input. Visual imagination forms a question-conditioned visual state through
visual queries with training-time generative supervision, while requiring no
pixel generation at inference.

Figure 4:Visual reflection for long-video understanding.The rendered
image is used only for visualization. The answer is conditioned directly on the
continuous visual queries at inference.

Figure 5:Comparison between visual imagination and textual reasoning.On this spatial task, textual reasoning produces a lengthy reasoning trace but
still predicts the wrong camera-motion direction, whereas visual imagination
reaches the correct answer with a compact visual state.

Figure 7:Visual Reconstruction Quality.Each example shows an input

Figure 11:Comparison between visual imagination and textual reasoning.On BLINK Counting, textual reasoning returns the correct count, whereas visual
